formation.title: The Unification of Scandinavia
formation.text:
The dream that Margaret I once held (a single crown uniting Denmark, Norway, and Sweden) has been realized anew. Where the Kalmar Union was undone by rivalry and distance, this Scandinavian realm stands on firmer foundations. From the herring-rich waters of the Sound to the iron mountains of Bergslagen, from the fjords of Norway to the forests of Finland, one people now speaks with one voice.

But what voice shall it be? Shall we look outward, as our Viking ancestors did, commanding the seas and building an empire of trade and sail? Or shall we look inward, binding our diverse peoples through the ancient tradition of the Thing, governance by assembly, law, and consent?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Our destiny lies upon the waves.

modifiers.name: Lords of the Northern Seas
modifiers.text: The united North commands the waters from the Arctic to the Baltic. Our keels cut every wave, our merchants fill every harbor, and our warships guard the narrow straits that all must pass.

options.text: Law and assembly shall unite us.

modifiers.name: All-Thing of the North
modifiers.text: From the ancient Thing assemblies to the council chambers of the union, Scandinavians have governed by consent and law. This realm is bound not by conquest alone but by shared custom and the voice of free men.

advances.name: Thing Assemblies
advances.text: The Scandinavian tradition of the Thing (open-air assemblies where free men gathered to settle disputes, declare law, and choose leaders) shaped governance across the Norse world.

advances.name: Viking Seamanship
advances.text: Generations of Norse seafaring skill, honed on the open Atlantic and Baltic, live on in the shipbuilding traditions and navigational knowledge of the Scandinavian peoples.

advances.name: Stave Church Tradition
advances.text: The wooden stave churches of Norway and Sweden, blending Christian devotion with Norse craftsmanship, stand as monuments to Scandinavia's unique cultural synthesis.

advances.name: Norse Runic Legacy
advances.text: The runic tradition of the North, from memorial stones to administrative records, fostered a culture of literacy and record-keeping that predates Latin learning in Scandinavia.

advances.name: Allodial Rights
advances.text: The Scandinavian tradition of odelsrett, the right of families to own and inherit land free from feudal obligation, created a class of independent freeholders unmatched in Europe. Every freeholder kept arms by law and answered the levy in person.

advances.name: Herring Markets
advances.text: The great herring markets of Scania drew merchants from across Northern Europe, making the salted herring trade one of the foundations of Scandinavian commerce.

advances.name: Bergslagen Ironworks
advances.text: The iron and copper mines of the Bergslagen district in central Sweden have supplied raw materials for tools, weapons, and export since the medieval period.

advances.name: Hanseatic Challenge
advances.text: By breaking the commercial stranglehold of the Hanseatic League, Scandinavian merchants established their own trading networks across the Baltic and North Sea.

advances.name: Nordic Law Codes
advances.text: The codification of Nordic provincial laws, from Magnus Lagabote's Norwegian national code to the Swedish provincial laws, created a unified legal framework for governance.

advances.name: Scandinavian Court Culture
advances.text: Renaissance learning and artistic patronage at the courts of Copenhagen and Stockholm fostered a distinctive Scandinavian cultural identity.

advances.name: Nordic Naval Yards
advances.text: Purpose-built royal shipyards at Copenhagen, Karlskrona, and other ports gave Scandinavia the capacity to build and maintain powerful Baltic fleets.

advances.name: Northern Reformation
advances.text: The adoption of Lutheranism across Scandinavia transformed the church into an instrument of state power while giving common people scripture in their own languages.

event.title: The Northern Reformation
event.text:
The winds of religious reform sweeping through Europe have found fertile ground in Scandinavia. Following the lead of Martin Luther, reformers like Hans Tausen in Denmark and Olaus Petri in Sweden have translated scripture into the vernacular tongues of the North. The old Catholic hierarchy, already weakened by distance from Rome and the independence of Nordic bishops, has crumbled before the new faith.

Christian III of Denmark and Gustav Vasa of Sweden have both seen the political advantages of reform, vast church lands can be seized for the crown, and national churches under royal control strengthen state authority. But the Reformation is more than a land grab. For common Scandinavians, hearing the Gospel in their own language for the first time is a profound spiritual experience.

How shall this united North shape its reformed church?

options.text: Let the Gospel be preached in every northern tongue.

modifiers.name: Reformation Zeal
modifiers.text: The pure word of the Gospel, preached in the tongues of the North, has swept away the old Latin church. Our people worship with renewed conviction.

options.text: The church's wealth belongs to the crown.

modifiers.name: Crown Over Church
modifiers.text: By seizing church lands and placing bishops under royal authority, the Scandinavian crown has gained vast wealth and unchallenged control over the spiritual life of the realm.

advances.name: Finnish Horse
advances.text: The huovit, mounted men kept at the crown's castles in Finland, ride small hardy horses on raids along the eastern frontier and strike before an enemy has formed. Their grandsons will be called the Hakkapeliitta.

advances.name: Baltic Dominion
advances.text: Scandinavian control of both shores of the Baltic Sea established the region as a Nordic lake, with diplomatic and naval power to match.

advances.name: The Great Copper Mountain
advances.text: The copper mine at Falun, producing two-thirds of Europe's copper at its peak, was called the realm's greatest fortification: its wealth financed Swedish wars and statecraft for centuries.

event.title: The Great Copper Mountain
event.text:
For centuries, the copper mine at Falun has been the treasury of the North. At its peak in the mid-seventeenth century, the Great Copper Mountain produced two-thirds of all the copper in Europe. The Privy Council called it the realm's strongest fortification (not of stone, but of coin. Swedish wars, diplomacy, and state-building were financed by Falun's endless seams of ore.

The fire-setting method) enormous bonfires lit deep underground to crack the rock, has carved out chambers of cathedral proportions. When the great cave-in of 1687 opened a pit visible for miles, it only revealed how much had already been extracted. The mine endures, a monument to Nordic industry and the patient extraction of wealth from unyielding stone.

options.text: The mountain's wealth serves the realm.

advances.name: Swedish Navy Expansion
advances.text: The expansion of the Swedish royal navy from a coastal defense force to a blue-water fleet capable of projecting power across the Baltic and beyond.

advances.name: Adelsvalde
advances.text: The age of noble dominance in Scandinavian politics, when the aristocracy controlled much of the land, the military, and the machinery of government.

advances.name: Timber Exports
advances.text: Scandinavia's vast forests provided Europe with lumber, tar, and naval stores, essential materials for the age of sail and the building boom of early modern cities.

advances.name: Crown Reduction
advances.text: Charles XI's reduktion, the systematic recovery of crown lands alienated to the nobility, restored royal finances and broke the power of the great magnates.

advances.name: Articles of War
advances.text: The articles of war are read to every company and bind officer and private to the same drill, the same prayers and the same punishments. Infantry trained under them holds its fire until the range is short and then goes in with the bayonet.

event.title: Cold Steel
event.text:
The articles of war have made one army of the realm's many regiments. The model is the army of Charles XI and Charles XII, whose soldiers were kept by the farms of their own province and drilled the year round.

On the battlefield that army rejected the European habit of standing volley fire. Its infantry advanced in silence under enemy musketry until close range, delivered a single volley and went in at once with bayonet and pike: the ga-pa doctrine. At Narva, eight thousand of them shattered a Russian army of forty thousand.

How shall Scandinavia carry this martial legacy forward?

options.text: The ga-pa shall break any line!

modifiers.name: Cold Steel
modifiers.text: Cold steel and an unflinching advance under fire have made Scandinavian infantry the terror of European battlefields.

options.text: The muster rolls are our true strength.

modifiers.name: Muster Discipline
modifiers.text: Every farm district keeps a soldier in peacetime and fields him in war. The realm can mobilize with remarkable speed and at small cost.

advances.name: Knektehållet
advances.text: By the contract of 1682 each province keeps a regiment of foot in perpetuity. Its farms are grouped into rotes, and every rote keeps one soldier and gives him a croft, so that a trained army is maintained cheaply in peace and mustered quickly for war.

advances.name: Line Ship Fleet
advances.text: The construction of dedicated ships of the line gave the Scandinavian navy the firepower to contest the great maritime powers in open battle.

advances.name: Scandinavian Absolutism
advances.text: The transition to absolute monarchy in Denmark-Norway and Sweden centralized state power, enabling ambitious building programs and administrative reform.

advances.name: Scandinavian East India Companies
advances.text: The Danish and Swedish East India Companies opened direct trade routes to Asia, importing tea, porcelain, and silk while establishing colonial outposts from Tranquebar to Canton.

advances.name: Nordic Enlightenment
advances.text: The Enlightenment in Scandinavia fostered scientific inquiry, university reform, and the expansion of literacy, building on the region's strong tradition of education.

advances.name: Freedom of the Press
advances.text: Sweden's 1766 Freedom of the Press Act, the world's first, established the principle that citizens have the right to publish and read without government censorship.

advances.name: Scandinavism
advances.text: The nineteenth-century movement of Scandinavism promoted cultural and political unity among the Nordic peoples, celebrating shared history, language, and identity.

advances.name: Industrial Modernization
advances.text:
The transformation of Scandinavia from an agrarian society to an industrial one, driven by mining, forestry, and the mechanization of traditional industries.

Available in: Bergslagen Forge

advances.name: Scandinavian Neutrality
advances.text: The Scandinavian tradition of armed neutrality, maintaining strong defenses while avoiding entanglement in great power conflicts, preserved independence through the upheavals of the Napoleonic era.

destiny.name: Scandinavian Destiny
destiny.text: The united North stands at a crossroads. With stability secured, the Scandinavian realm can now pursue its chosen destiny, whether mastery of the seas or the perfection of governance by assembly.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Scandinavian Destiny
event.text:
The Scandinavian realm has achieved a stability that the Kalmar Union never knew. Where that older union was plagued by succession crises and Swedish revolts, this kingdom rests on firmer ground. Now the question turns from survival to ambition: what shall this united North become?

The choice made at our founding set the course. Now, with stability secured, the first steps of that destiny can begin.

destiny.name: Mastery of the Sound
destiny.text: Seize control of Lubeck and the Oresund narrows. Hold Helsingor, where Eric of Pomerania collected the Sound Dues under the walls of Krogen, and channel the wealth of every vessel that passes between the North Sea and the Baltic through Scandinavian hands.

conditions.text: Chose the Lords of the Northern Seas destiny
Own Lübeck, or a subject owns it
Own Helsingør, or a subject owns it

event.title: Mastery of the Sound
event.text:
The Oresund, that narrow passage between Helsingborg and Helsingor, has been called the Golden Gate of the North. Every vessel passing from the North Sea to the Baltic must thread this needle, and now both shores belong to Scandinavia. With Lubeck itself brought under our control, the Hanseatic merchants who once dictated terms to Nordic kings now trade at our sufferance.

The Sound Toll, once a modest Danish levy, can now become the foundation of Scandinavian maritime supremacy. Every cask of herring, every bolt of cloth, every ingot of iron that moves between east and west pays tribute to the Northern Crown.

destiny.name: Dominion Over the North Sea
destiny.text: Reclaim the old Norse territories of Scotland and Orkney. With Edinburgh under the Northern banner and gold flowing through the treasury, the North Sea becomes a Scandinavian highway once more.

conditions.text: Own Edinburgh, or a subject owns it
Own Orkney, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: Dominion Over the North Sea
event.text:
The North Sea, once the highway of Viking raiders, is again a Scandinavian lake. Edinburgh, seat of Scottish kings, flies the Northern banner, and the Orkney Islands have returned to Norse rule after centuries under the Scottish crown. Gold flows through our markets, funding the warships and merchant vessels that enforce our claim.

British and Dutch traders eye our growing fleet with alarm. Two visions emerge among the admiralty: shall we build warships to rule by force, or merchantmen to rule by profit?

modifiers.name: War Fleet Supremacy
modifiers.text: The Scandinavian admiralty builds warships to dominate the North Sea by force. Naval bases from Bergen to Edinburgh project power across the Atlantic approaches.

modifiers.name: Merchant Marine Dominion
modifiers.text: Scandinavian merchantmen crowd every harbor from Archangel to Lisbon. Northern traders control the flow of goods through the straits and across the open sea.

destiny.name: The Northern Empire
destiny.text: Reach from Novgorod to Greenland: the Varangian route reborn and the abandoned western settlements reclaimed. Build the East Indiamen of the Danish and Swedish companies in two shipyards of the realm, and build a colonial office to coordinate a realm that straddles oceans.

conditions.text: Own Novgorod, or a subject owns it
Own Brattahlid, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 75
Has a Dry Dock, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard or Naval Base in at least 2 locations

event.title: The Northern Empire
event.text:
From Edinburgh to Novgorod, from Brattahlid to the Baltic, the Northern Empire stretches across the known world. The Varangian route, that ancient path from Scandinavia to Byzantium, is reborn under a single crown. In the west, the Greenland settlements, abandoned for centuries, have been reclaimed.

This is a realm that straddles oceans and continents. Shall we embrace our role as a true thalassocracy, a maritime empire governed from the quarterdeck, or shall we honor the Norse settlers who first carved civilization from Greenland's ice, and build an empire of colonists and homesteaders?

modifiers.name: Northern Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: A maritime empire governed from the quarterdeck. Scandinavian admirals command fleets that patrol from Greenland to Novgorod, enforcing the Northern Crown's dominion over every sea lane.

options.text: We settle where the sea carries us.

modifiers.name: Settler Empire
modifiers.text: Where the sea carries Scandinavians, they build. From Greenland to distant colonies, Nordic settlers carve new homesteads from the wilderness, carrying their laws and customs to new lands.

destiny.name: The Law of the North
destiny.text: Establish the foundations of Scandinavian governance. Spread the legal traditions of the Thing across the realm with a Tingsted or a council hall in three towns, and build up Uppsala, seat of the archbishop and home of the law of Uppland.

conditions.text: Chose the All-Thing of the North destiny
Has a Tingsted, Local Council, Council Hall or Expanded Council Hall in at least 3 locations
Stability at least 25
We own Uppsala and its development is at least 24

event.title: The Law of the North
event.text:
The ancient tradition of the Thing, governance by assembly and consent, has been renewed across the Scandinavian realm. Where medieval law codes once served individual provinces, a unified legal tradition now binds the entire North. Banking institutions fund the construction of courts and schools in every corner of the kingdom, and Uppsala, seat of the archbishop and home of the law of Uppland, has grown with them.

The allodial rights that protect Nordic freeholders are no longer mere custom but codified law. Prosperity grows as secure property rights and consistent justice attract settlement and trade. The foundations of modern Scandinavian governance are being laid, not by conquest, but by consensus.

options.text: The law speaks for all free men.

destiny.name: The Riksdag Ascendant
destiny.text: Teach one in five of the realm's people to read, so that printed debates carry Nordic ideas of governance to every corner of the realm. Build Stockholm up into a capital fit to seat the estates, and fill the treasury to fund a modern legislative assembly.

conditions.text: Average country literacy at least 20
We own Stockholm and its development is at least 34
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Riksdag Ascendant
event.text:
The Scandinavian Riksdag, evolved from the ancient Thing assemblies into a modern deliberative body, has become the most powerful legislature in Northern Europe. The printing press carries its debates to every literate household, and Stockholm has grown into a capital fit to seat the four estates.

Debates rage in the assembly hall. Progressive voices demand that the Riksdag drive innovation and modernization. Conservative members argue that the body's true strength lies in balancing the estates and preserving harmony among the realm's diverse peoples.

modifiers.name: Riksdag Reforms
modifiers.text: The Riksdag drives a program of modernization, reforming administration, promoting innovation, and extending representative governance to every corner of the realm.

options.text: The Riksdag shall balance the estates.

modifiers.name: Estate Harmony
modifiers.text: The Riksdag's genius lies not in radical change but in balancing the interests of nobles, clergy, burghers, and peasants, maintaining harmony among diverse estates through careful deliberation.

destiny.name: Beacon of Liberty
destiny.text: Become the Enlightenment's model state. Teach two in five of the realm's people to read, make Copenhagen the first city of the North, twice the town it was, and win the prestige to show that liberty and order are not opposites but complements. Build a Riksdagshus worthy of the world's most advanced legislature.

conditions.text: Average country literacy at least 40
We own Copenhagen and its development is at least 50
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: Beacon of Liberty
event.text:
The Nordic model has become the envy of Europe. Philosophers cite Scandinavian governance as proof that liberty and order are not opposites but complements. The Freedom of the Press Act, the world's first, has been extended across the realm, and Enlightenment ideals find their fullest expression in Northern institutions.

Two visions compete for the soul of this Northern beacon: shall we formalize our governance in a written constitution, establishing rights that no monarch can revoke? Or shall we use our moral authority to mediate the conflicts of Europe, becoming the peaceful arbiter of nations?

options.text: We shall write the rights of all Northmen.

modifiers.name: Constitutional Charter
modifiers.text: A written constitution enshrines the rights of Scandinavian citizens. No monarch may revoke what the people's representatives have established in law.

options.text: We shall arbitrate the peace of nations.

modifiers.name: Arbiter of Nations
modifiers.text: Scandinavia's moral authority, built on centuries of representative governance and religious tolerance, makes it the natural mediator of European disputes.

units.name: Langskip
units.text: Fast, shallow-draft warships descended from Viking longship design, built for raiding and coastal patrol in the narrow waters of the North.

units.name: Langskip Crew
units.text: Levied longship crews drawn from coastal communities with centuries of seafaring tradition.

units.name: Huovi
units.text: Castle horsemen of the Finnish frontier on small, hardy mounts. They are quick to strike and at home in the forest, and too lightly protected for a long melee.

units.name: Bondeuppbåd
units.text: Free farmers called out under the old provincial laws, each bringing the shield, spear and crossbow he is bound to keep at home. They fight for land that is their own, and they fight without armour.

units.name: Adelsfana
units.text: The banner of the nobility: armoured horsemen with wheel-lock pistols, furnished by noble estates in return for their freedom from tax.

units.name: Orlogsskib
units.text: A fast Scandinavian warship designed for both Baltic patrol and open-sea combat, balancing firepower with the speed needed to dominate narrow straits.

units.name: Carolean
units.text: Elite Swedish-style infantry trained in the ga-pa doctrine, disciplined advance under fire followed by a devastating bayonet charge at close range.

units.name: Legd Soldiers
units.text: Soldiers sent by the legds, groups of farms that each find, clothe and keep one man. They drill at the church green after the Sunday service and march when the realm calls.

units.name: Linjeskip
units.text: A Scandinavian ship of the line, faster than its European counterparts, designed for the shallow Baltic waters where maneuverability matters as much as broadside weight.

buildings.name: Stave Church
buildings.text: Wooden churches built with the Norse post-and-lintel technique, decorated with intricate carvings that blend Christian imagery with ancient Nordic motifs.

buildings.name: Bergslagen Forge
buildings.text: An ironworks in the Bergslagen tradition, smelting high-quality osmund iron from Swedish ore using charcoal-fueled blast furnaces.

buildings.name: Orlogsvarvet
buildings.text: A royal naval shipyard built in the Scandinavian tradition, with covered drydocks and slipways for constructing warships year-round.

buildings.name: Tingsted
buildings.text: A formal assembly hall continuing the ancient Thing tradition, where local representatives gather to deliberate on law, taxation, and governance.

buildings.name: Herring Saltery
buildings.text: A coastal facility for salting and barreling herring in the Scanian tradition, producing preserved fish for export across Northern Europe.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Koppargruva
buildings.text: A copper extraction facility using the fire-setting method pioneered at Falun, enormous underground fires crack the ore-bearing rock for extraction.

where.text: The location's raw material is Copper

buildings.name: East India Kontor
buildings.text: A trading house modeled on the Danish and Swedish East India Companies, handling the import and resale of Asian luxury goods.

buildings.name: Soldattorp
buildings.text: A soldier's croft. The farms of a district keep one soldier between them and give him a cottage, a field and a cow, which he works between musters. Only the realm's own provinces carry the allotment.

buildings.name: Colonial Admiralty
buildings.text: A combined naval command and trading headquarters for coordinating Scandinavian colonial ventures, modeled on the great admiralties of the maritime powers.

buildings.name: Riksdagshus
buildings.text: A grand assembly hall in the Nordic parliamentary tradition, where representatives of the estates gather to deliberate on law, taxation, and the governance of the realm.

list.name: Kalmar Riksråd
list.text: The joint Council of the Realm of the three Nordic kingdoms, descended from the magnates' assembly Margaret I summoned to Kalmar in June 1397 to crown Erik of Pomerania. Each kingdom's riksråd seated its bishops, its great lay magnates, and the commanders of its strongest castles: Akershus and Bergenhus in Norway, Stockholm and Kalmar in Sweden, Roskilde and Copenhagen in Denmark. The councils ratified kings, mediated succession disputes, and clung to the principle that the realm should be administered by its own dignitaries under its own laws, a brake on royal centralization that union monarchs from Margaret to Christian II resented and tried to circumvent.

list.name: Sound Dues
list.text: The Øresundstolden, a toll on every foreign keel passing through the narrow strait between Helsingør and Helsingborg, decreed by Erik of Pomerania in 1429. From the great fortress of Kronborg, Danish gunners enforced compliance over centuries: a ship that refused to halt could be sunk in mid-channel. Reformed in 1567 from a per-ship fee into a one-to-two-percent ad valorem tax on cargo value, the Sound Dues at their height furnished up to two-thirds of Danish state revenue and made every European trading nation a reluctant tributary of the northern crown.

conditions.text: Owns Helsingør

list.name: Riksdag of the Estates
list.text: The Riksens Ständer, the Swedish parliament of four estates, traced to the assembly Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson convened at Arboga in January 1435 during his rebellion against the Kalmar union. Where most European parliaments seated three estates, the Nordic body uniquely included a fourth (bondeståndet, the free peasants of the realm) alongside nobles, clergy, and burghers. Formalized under Gustav Vasa in 1527 and constitutionalized after 1719, the four-estate Riksdag gave the Scandinavian commons a voice in legislation found nowhere else in Europe and bound the monarchy to govern by consent of the full realm.

list.name: Len System
list.text: The late-medieval system of provincial administration through which the Nordic crown delegated rule to lensherrer holding royal castles (Akershus at Oslo, Bergenhus at Bergen, Aalborghus in northern Jutland, Stockholm in Sweden) in exchange for revenue, soldiers, and oaths of fealty. Beneath each lensherre, the lensmænd were lower royal officials who collected taxes, mustered the bondelevy, judged petty cases, and represented the king at the bygdeting. The len system bound the realm together at low cost but created a class of magnates whose castles, men, and revenues could turn against the crown at the next succession dispute.

list.name: Reduktion
list.text: The recurring Nordic act of crown reclamation, by which alienated lands were resumed from those who held them. Gustav Vasa's reduktion, ratified at the Diet of Västerås in 1527, transferred to the Swedish crown the church estates that had constituted twenty-one percent of the realm's land, producing nearly forty percent of state revenue by mid-century and underwriting the rise of a centralized monarchy. The pattern repeated under Karl XI's Great Reduktion after 1680, this time at the expense of the high nobility. Whether aimed at bishops or barons, reduktion left a long memory of fear among those whose estates rested on royal grant.

conditions.text: Stability at least 0

list.name: Hanseatic Kontor
list.text: The Tyskebryggen at Bergen, last and northernmost of the four great Hanseatic kontors, established around 1350 as a private corporate enclave of German merchants enjoying their own treasury, court, legislation, and seal under Norwegian sovereignty. The kontor's two thousand Hansards held a near-monopoly on the export of stockfish from the Lofoten fisheries, paying a low duty of roughly 148 kilos of grain per ship and trading under their own laws on Norwegian soil. Its wharves enriched the realm's customs but locked native burghers out of the Atlantic trade for four centuries: the kontor was not closed in favor of Norwegian merchants until 1754.

list.name: Bremerholm Admiralty
list.text: The dedicated naval base founded by King Hans of Denmark in 1510 on the islet of Bremerholm in Copenhagen harbor, named for the merchants and shipwrights from Bremen who first worked there. Christian IV expanded it into a vast complex of slipways, ropewalks, mast-cranes, and quarters for officers, and from 1690 the operation spilled across the channel to Nyholm. The fleet itself was crewed by udskrevne søfolk (coastal peasants conscripted by lot from the maritime parishes of Denmark and Norway under royal naval ordinance), a corvée resented by the fishing villages that supplied it but indispensable to a navy that policed the Sound and the Baltic.
